| CORE-025 | P0 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Context terminal state | `DatabaseContext` does not override `ValidateCanCreateContainer`, and its connection/transaction entry points do not consistently call `ThrowIfDisposed`. After disposal, `AcquireSlot` sees nulled governors and returns an ungoverned default slot, so a container created either before or after disposal can create a fresh physical connection and execute outside the context's admission controls. | **Resolved:** `DatabaseContext` now overrides `ValidateCanCreateContainer()` to call `ThrowIfDisposed()` (rejects `CreateSqlContainer` immediately post-disposal); `GetStandardConnectionWithExecutionType` — the entry point every connection-acquisition path ultimately reaches — now calls `ThrowIfDisposed()` first. `AcquireSlot`/`AcquireInfrastructureSlot`'s null-governor fallback now throws `ObjectDisposedException` instead of silently returning an ungoverned default slot — but **only when `IsDisposed`**: a null governor is also the legitimate state during the narrow bootstrap window before `InitializePoolGovernors()` has run (`_effectivePoolGovernorEnabled` defaults to `true` specifically so the very first, pre-governor connection during construction still reaches this code) — conflating the two states initially caused a real regression (24 test failures constructing contexts) that surfaced immediately on the first full-suite run after implementing, fixed by adding the `IsDisposed` distinction via a new `ThrowIfGovernorMissingAfterDisposal()` helper. | CORE-026 | P0 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Context disposal/lease ownership | Disposal waits for governors to drain only for `PoolAcquireTimeout`. On timeout it logs and continues to dispose owned data sources and release unique-connection claims even though commands/readers may still own permits and physical connections. The context can therefore return while old work remains alive and another context can claim the same connection identity. | **Resolved via "defer dependent cleanup," the third option in the completion criteria's shutdown-policy list** (not "safely cancel/abort" — no cancellation mechanism exists for in-flight ADO.NET commands, and forcing one was judged out of scope). `DisposePoolGovernors()`/`Async` now call `governor.Close()` on both governors *before* draining either (closing admission atomically first — see CORE-027), and return `false` if any governor times out draining instead of just logging. `DisposeManaged()`/`DisposeManagedAsync()` now only call `DisposeOwnedDataSources()` and `UniqueConnectionStringRegistry.ReleaseAll`/`UnregisterAllForWarning` when every governor drained cleanly; on a timeout they log a warning and skip that cleanup entirely — leaking the data source/claim rather than risking tearing down a resource an outstanding lease still depends on. | CORE-027 | P0 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Governor shutdown race | `PoolGovernor` has no closed/draining admission state. `WaitForDrainAsync` only observes `_inUse == 0`; a caller that captured the governor reference can acquire after the drain signal or race semaphore disposal. Nulling the context fields does not close the governor itself. | **Resolved.** `PoolGovernor` now extends `SafeAsyncDisposableBase` (per user suggestion mid-session, replacing an initial manual `_disposedOnce` `Interlocked` guard that duplicated what the base class already provides — matches the convention every other disposable type in this codebase already follows) instead of implementing bare `IDisposable`. Added `Close()`/`IsClosed` (independent of `IsDisposed` — `Close()` can run ahead of actual teardown to stop admission before draining) and a `ThrowIfClosed()` check at the top of all four acquire entry points (`Acquire`, `TryAcquire`, `AcquireAsync`, `TryAcquireAsync`), each throwing `ObjectDisposedException` immediately rather than either succeeding past intended shutdown or failing deep inside torn-down semaphore machinery. `DisposeManaged()` (overriding the base's template method instead of a raw `Dispose()`) calls `Close()` first, so `WaitForDrainAsync` now has a real guarantee once combined with a `Close()` call before draining begins: `_inUse` can only decrease, never increase. Tests: `PoolGovernorTests.cs` (7 new tests — closed-then-acquire for all 4 entry points, close-prevents-new-admission-so-drain-completes, dispose-is-idempotent, dispose-closes-admission). **Residual, deliberately out of scope** (same class of TOCTOU as CORE-023's residual note): a caller that already read a governor reference and is about to call an acquire method has no protection between that read and the call itself — closing this fully would need every acquire path to hold a coordinating lock across the check, a larger change not attempted here. Full suite green (7378 tests). |
| CORE-028 | P0 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Constructor failure ownership | `InitializeReadOnlyConnectionResources` can create internally owned writer and reader `DbDataSource` instances before later validation, governor setup, session initialization, and unique-claim steps. The outer constructor catch cleans persistent connections/governors and warning registrations but never disposes those data sources. Since no context is returned, these provider resources can leak permanently on construction failure. | **Resolved by reusing the existing `DisposeOwnedDataSources()` method** (already correctly distinguishes caller-supplied from internally-created data sources via `_dataSourceProvided`, and already de-duplicates when reader/writer share one instance) rather than building a new ownership-scope abstraction — added a call to it in both the inner catch (around `ClaimUniqueConnectionStrings`) and the outer constructor catch. | CORE-029 | P0 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Exception identity under admission control | Discovered while writing TEST-001 (two-tenant failure containment). `PoolSaturatedException` and `ModeContentionException` both extend `TimeoutException` directly and are documented (`ModeContentionException`, explicitly, in this file's own Exception Hierarchy section) as NOT part of the `DatabaseException` hierarchy — "a `catch (DatabaseException)` will not catch it." But `SqlContainer`'s `catch (Exception ex) when (ex is not DatabaseException && IsTimeout(ex))` clause treats any `TimeoutException`-derived exception as a raw provider timeout and translates it into `CommandTimeoutException` (a `DatabaseException` subclass) via the dialect's exception translator — silently destroying that documented type-identity contract whenever either exception originates from inside an actual command execution (`ExecuteNonQueryAsync`/`ExecuteReaderAsync`/`ExecuteScalarAsync` all share this code path), as opposed to, e.g., `BeginTransaction`, which never reaches it and was already correctly covered by an existing test. | **Resolved:** `SqlContainer.IsTimeout(Exception)` now returns `false` immediately for `PoolSaturatedException`/`ModeContentionException`, so both fall through to the existing (correct) `catch (Exception ex) when (ex is not DatabaseException)` clause, which already rethrows a non-`DbException` unchanged via `throw;` — a one-line, single-point-of-truth fix since both call sites (`ExecuteNonQueryAsync`, `ExecuteReaderAsyncInternal`) share this one helper. Tests: `InfrastructureTimeoutExceptionIdentityTests.PoolSaturatedException_PropagatesUnwrapped_FromCommandExecution_NotTranslatedToCommandTimeoutException` (saturates a `MaxConcurrentWrites=1` writer governor, asserts `ExecuteNonQueryAsync` throws `PoolSaturatedException` itself, not `CommandTimeoutException`) and `..._ModeContentionException_PropagatesUnwrapped_FromOrdinaryOpDuringActiveTransaction_..." (holds a `SingleConnection` transaction open, asserts an ordinary concurrent `ExecuteScalarOrNullAsync` throws `ModeContentionException` itself); both confirmed genuinely red first (both threw `CommandTimeoutException` with the real exception demoted to `InnerException`). Also fixed `TwoTenantFailureContainmentTests` (TEST-001, written first and what surfaced this bug) to assert `PoolSaturatedException` propagates as originally designed, replacing its interim `TotalSlotTimeouts` assertion (which turned out to depend on which of `PoolGovernor`'s two internal rejection paths — queue-depth overflow vs. genuine wait-timeout — fired, not the actual point of the test) with `InUse`/`TotalAcquired` assertions that hold regardless of which rejection path is hit. Full suite green (7396 tests, both net8.0/net10.0) — no other test anywhere depended on the old wrapping behavior. |
| CORE-030 | P0 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Metrics integrity — broken-connection double-count | Discovered while writing TEST-014 (exact metrics lifecycle) — a genuinely different mechanism from the CORE-022 false positive. `TrackedConnection.HandleMetricsStateChange` correctly counts a `Broken` transition as a close, but `DisposeConnectionSync`/`DisposeConnectionAsyncCore`'s own guard (`if (_connection.State != ConnectionState.Closed)`) treats `Broken` as "still needs closing" and calls `CloseWithMetrics()` → `_connection.Close()` again. `Broken → Closed` is a real, distinct ADO.NET state transition (not a no-op even on real providers, since `OriginalState != CurrentState`), so it fires a second `StateChange` event, which `HandleMetricsStateChange` counts as a *second* close for the same physical connection's single lifecycle — permanently inflating `ConnectionsClosed` relative to `ConnectionsOpened` every time a connection breaks and is later disposed (the normal, expected disposal path for a broken connection, not a rare edge case). | **Resolved:** added a `_closeAlreadyCountedForThisOpen` flag to `TrackedConnection`, reset to `0` on the `Open` transition, set via `Interlocked.Exchange` on the first `Closed`-or-`Broken` transition per open cycle; a second transition into either state before the next `Open` is a no-op for counting purposes (the connection's resources still get disposed normally — only the metrics double-count is suppressed). Test: `DatabaseMetricsTests.Metrics_ConnectionBreaksWhileHeld_CountsExactlyOneClose_NotZeroOrTwo` opens a connection, force-breaks it directly (`fakeDbConnection.BreakConnection()`), then disposes it through the normal `CloseAndDisposeConnection` path, asserting `ConnectionsClosed` is exactly 2 (matching `ConnectionsOpened=2`, one from context construction's own dialect-detection connection, one from the test's own) at every step — including after the redundant dispose-time close, where the bug previously pushed it to 3; confirmed genuinely red first. A companion test, `Metrics_ConnectionFailsToOpen_LeavesOpenCloseCountsUnchanged`, proves the *different* failed-open case was already correct (a connection whose `Open()` throws before reaching `ConnectionState.Open` never fires a `StateChange` at all, so it was never at risk of this bug) — passed immediately, no fix needed there. Full suite green (7409 tests, both net8.0/net10.0). |
| CORE-031 | P2 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Public API leakage — `ILockerAsync` | Cross-checked against an external analysis document (not a bug per se, but a confirmed public-surface finding): every implementation (`RealAsyncLocker`, `ReusableAsyncLocker`, `NoOpAsyncLocker`) is `internal sealed`, and its only consumer, `ITrackedConnection.GetLock()`, is itself declared on an `internal` interface. A consumer can never obtain, construct, or meaningfully implement one — it was pure public surface with zero legitimate external reachability, contradicting CLAUDE.md's own "minimize public APIs; make types/members internal when possible" principle. | **Resolved:** changed `ILockerAsync` (`pengdows.crud.abstractions/threading/ILockerAsync.cs`) from `public interface` to `internal interface`. `InternalsVisibleTo("pengdows.crud")` already existed on the abstractions assembly, so no new visibility wiring was needed. Test: `PublicApiSurfaceLeakageTests.ILockerAsync_IsNotPublic` (reflection assertion); confirmed genuinely red first. Regenerated the `interface-api-check` baseline (`dotnet run --project tools/interface-api-check ... --generate`, 448 → 436 entries — 4 signatures removed: the interface plus its 3 members). Full suite green (7420 tests, both net8.0/net10.0), full solution build clean including `testbed`/`stormgate`/`opentelemetry` (none reference this type). |
| CORE-032 | P2 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Public API leakage — `IConnectionLocalState` | Same audit. Mutator methods (`DisablePrepare()`, `Reset()`, `MarkShapePrepared()`) are internal prepared-statement bookkeeping a consumer should never call directly, and the only exposure point, `ITrackedConnection.LocalState`, is itself on an `internal` interface. The concrete `ConnectionLocalState` class was also `public` for the same no-reason. | **Resolved:** changed `IConnectionLocalState` (`pengdows.crud.abstractions/connection/IConnectionLocalState.cs`) and `ConnectionLocalState` (`pengdows.crud/connection/ConnectionLocalState.cs`) from `public` to `internal`. Tests: `PublicApiSurfaceLeakageTests.IConnectionLocalState_IsNotPublic` and `ConnectionLocalState_IsNotPublic`; confirmed genuinely red first. Same baseline regeneration as CORE-031 (8 more signatures removed: interface, 2 properties, 5 methods). Full suite green (7420 tests, both net8.0/net10.0). |
| CORE-033 | — | **Investigated, rejected (2026-08-29)** | `SafeAsyncDisposableBase` — NOT leakage | The same external document flagged `SafeAsyncDisposableBase` (the concrete base class) as public-surface leakage with "no documented consumer-subclassing story." | **Rejected after investigation — do not attempt this again.** `SqlContainer`, `ContextBase` (the base of `DatabaseContext` itself), and `TenantContextRegistry` are all genuinely, deliberately public per CLAUDE.md's API Visibility Principles ("Public constructors are allowed for core entry points... and tenant helpers"), and all three derive from `SafeAsyncDisposableBase`. C# requires a base class to be at least as accessible as its derived classes (`CS0060`), so internalizing it is impossible without also internalizing those three intentional public types. Attempted the change, hit the compiler error immediately, reverted. Not every candidate in the external document held up — this is the one confirmed false claim discovered while acting on the batch (a second one, the `ISafeAsyncDisposableBase` *interface* being legitimate, was already caught during the earlier verification pass and never attempted as code). |
| CORE-034 | P2 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Public API leakage — `TypeCoercionOptions` | Same audit. `TypeCoercionOptions` is never accepted or returned by anything in `pengdows.crud.abstractions`. Its only "public" consumer, `TypeCoercionHelper.Coerce(...)`, is itself declared on an `internal static class` — a public member's effective accessibility is capped by its containing type, so it was not actually reachable either. No public constructor parameter or settable property anywhere let a consumer supply a custom instance, so the type provided zero real configurability despite being public (its `JsonPreference` field is also fully dead — never read anywhere in the codebase, public or internal). | **Resolved:** changed `TypeCoercionOptions` (`pengdows.crud/TypeCoercionOptions.cs`) from `public sealed record` to `internal sealed record`. This is a plain concrete class (not tracked by `interface-api-check`, which only tracks `pengdows.crud.abstractions` interfaces), so no baseline regeneration was needed for this one. Left `JsonPreference` in place rather than also removing the dead field in the same change — now that the type is internal, that's an ordinary internal-cleanup call rather than a public-breaking-change one, and out of scope for this pass. Test: `PublicApiSurfaceLeakageTests.TypeCoercionOptions_IsNotPublic`; confirmed genuinely red first. Full suite green (7420 tests, both net8.0/net10.0). |

| TEST-017 | P0 | **Done, correctly scoped (2026-08-30)** | Constructor rollback matrix | With disposable fake native data sources, inject failure after writer-source creation, reader-source creation, read-only validation, governor creation, session initialization, and uniqueness claim. CORE-028's `Construction_FailsClaimingUniqueConnectionString_DisposesInternallyCreatedDataSource` already proved the "internally owned resources unwind" half at the uniqueness-claim failure point. `Construction_FailsClaimingUniqueConnectionString_DoesNotDisposeCallerSuppliedDataSource` proves the flip side — a `DbDataSource` supplied through the public `DatabaseContext(configuration, dataSource, factory, loggerFactory)` overload is never disposed by a failed construction. **New (2026-08-29, this session): two more of the six named gaps closed.** (1) **Session initialization** — `Construction_SessionInitializationFails_DisposesPersistentConnectionAndPropagates` uses `fakeDbFactory.SetCommandFailure(exactSessionSettingsText, exception)`, matched by exact command text (learned via a non-failing probe construction first, not hardcoded/guessed dialect SQL) so only the session-settings command fails, not the earlier dialect-detection probes sharing the same persistent connection under `DbMode.SingleConnection`; asserts the wrapping `ConnectionException` carries the injected exception as `InnerException` and every created connection was disposed. Passed immediately — no bug found, this is already-correct behavior. (2) **"Original exception preserved when cleanup itself throws"** — no longer just "verifiable by inspection": `Construction_FailsAndCleanupDataSourceDisposeThrows_OriginalExceptionStillPropagates` uses a new `fakeDbFactory.ThrowOnDataSourceDispose` hook (paired with a new `FakeDbDataSource.ThrowOnDispose` property) to make an internally-created `DbDataSource` throw during cleanup while construction fails for an unrelated, pre-existing reason (`EnforceUniqueConnectionString`); confirmed genuinely red by temporarily removing `DatabaseContext.DisposeOwnedDataSources()`'s own internal per-item `try/catch` (its `catch { // ignore }` around `primaryOwned?.Dispose()`) — this, not the outer constructor catch's swallow, is the layer actually responsible for the guarantee; the outer catch's own swallow (initially suspected and temporarily disabled first) turned out not to be reached at all for this failure path, since `ClaimUniqueConnectionStrings`'s own inner catch calls `DisposeOwnedDataSources()` directly. Restored both guards after confirming red; full suite green afterward. **New (2026-08-30, this session): read-only validation closed; writer/reader-source creation reclassified from "deferred" to "no seam exists" after direct verification — this is a correction, not new deferral.** (3) **Read-only validation** — `Construction_ReadOnlyValidationFails_PropagatesConnectionFailedException` uses a new `fakeDbFactory.SetFailOnOpenForConnectionString(connectionString, exception)` hook (connection-string-scoped, unlike the factory-wide `ConnectionFailureMode.FailOnOpen`) so only the distinct `ReadOnlyConnectionString`'s connection fails `Open()`, not the earlier writer-side connections built during dialect detection/session setup; the exact connection string was learned via a non-failing probe construction first, same pattern as the session-initialization test. Confirmed genuinely red first by disabling the new hook (`Assert.Throws` failed with "no exception was thrown"), then confirmed green after re-enabling; asserts `TestConnect`'s `ConnectionFailedException` carries the injected exception as `InnerException` with `Phase="ReadOnlyValidation"`/`Role="ReadOnly"`. **Writer-source creation and reader-source creation fault injection are reclassified: NOT a fakeDb testability gap, same category as governor creation.** Direct reading of `TryCreateDataSource`/`TryCreateProviderDataSource` (`DatabaseContext.Initialization.cs`) shows the reflected provider-native `CreateDataSource` call is wrapped in two layers of catch — a targeted `TargetInvocationException`-wrapping-`NotSupportedException` catch, then an unconditional `catch (Exception ex)` that logs at Debug and returns `null` for *any other* exception — after which `TryCreateDataSource` always falls through to the `GenericDbDataSource` wrapper, which is itself wrapped in its own catch-all returning `null` on failure. No exception thrown from a data-source-creation attempt (via any test double, fakeDb included) can propagate past this by design; construction proceeds with a `null` data source instead (handled gracefully at both call sites, lines ~1391 and ~1420) rather than failing. This makes "inject a failure at writer/reader-source creation and prove construction rolls back" architecturally unreachable today, not a fakeDb infrastructure gap — the earlier "deferred, not attempted" framing for these two specifically undersold how settled this is; there is no seam here to add fakeDb support for. Governor creation remains unreachable for the same reason it always was (pure in-process `SemaphoreSlim` construction, no I/O, no existing injection seam), consistent with the project's precedent for this class of decision (e.g. CORE-023/CORE-027's residual notes). All four of TEST-017's six named phases are now either covered by a real test (uniqueness claim, session initialization, read-only validation) or honestly documented as having no fault-injection seam to close (writer-source creation, reader-source creation, governor creation) — nothing remains in a "deferred, someday" state. Full suite green (7455 tests, both net8.0/net10.0). |

| DOC-014 | P0 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Tenant identity and rotation contract | Define tenant-ID case/normalization rules and the concurrency semantics of re-registration, invalidation, in-flight requests, disposal, and generation changes. | DOC-016 | P1 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Cache security and cardinality | Inventory process-wide and gateway caches, their keys, bounds, eviction, tenant/version cardinality, secret handling, and collision guarantees. This matters directly to long-lived multi-tenant processes. **Closed:** new `docs/cache-and-context-contract.md` inventories every cache (`DataReaderMapper`'s three static caches, `BaseTableGateway`'s `_readerPlans`/`_columnListCache`/dialect-fingerprint-keyed `_queryCache`+`_whereParameterNames`, `TypeMapRegistry._typeMap`, `ConnectionStringNormalizationCache`) with key/scope/bound/secret-handling for each. **Found a real, previously-undocumented growth risk while researching, not just a doc gap:** `BaseTableGateway._wrappedTableNameCache` (`ConcurrentDictionary<ISqlDialect, string>`) is a **plain, unbounded dictionary** keyed by dialect *instance* — unlike every sibling cache, which is either a bounded `BoundedCache` or fingerprint-keyed. Since every `IDatabaseContext` gets its own dialect instance, a singleton gateway serving a multi-tenant process with tenant rotation (re-register + invalidate, per `multitenancy-architecture.md`) accumulates one permanent, never-evicted entry per rotation — a slow memory leak in any process that rotates tenants over its lifetime. Documented in the new doc's inventory table and flagged there for a future CORE-level fix (fingerprint-keying like `_queryCache`, or bounding it); not fixed in this doc-only pass. Also confirmed `TypeMapRegistry` is per-`DatabaseContext`-instance by default (a redundancy tradeoff across tenants, not a leak — a shared-registry constructor overload exists for callers who want to avoid the redundant computation). |
| DOC-017 | P0 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Transaction concurrency contract | State whether concurrent use is supported, serialized, or rejected. Cover active readers, commit/rollback/dispose races, savepoints, cancellation, mode locks, and ownership of the pinned connection. Documentation must match enforced behavior. **Closed (2026-08-29, this session):** added a "Concurrency contract" section to `docs/transactions.md` (expanded the existing doc rather than fragmenting into a new file), verified against current `TransactionContext.cs`/`ReusableAsyncLocker.cs` source rather than assumed from the tracker's CORE-023 summary. States plainly: `TransactionContext` is single-flow by design — ordinary concurrent commands serialize (block, no timeout) through one internal lock; an open reader holds that lock for its whole lifetime and makes every other operation (command, commit, rollback, savepoint, dispose) fail fast with `InvalidOperationException` naming the reader, from either the same flow or a different thread, rather than deadlock; a `Commit`/`Rollback` race has exactly one winner with the connection released exactly once; `Dispose` never tears down a transaction another thread is actively completing; a pre-cancelled token leaves the transaction fully untouched and unwrapped (`OperationCanceledException`, retryable with a fresh token); savepoints share the identical lock as ordinary commands; `DbMode.SingleConnection`'s separate transaction gate is a no-op under every other mode; and `GetConnection`'s `ExecutionType` parameter has no effect (always the one pinned connection). Every claim cites the exact proving test (`TransactionReaderLockLifetimeTests`, `TransactionCompletionReaderGuardTests`, `TransactionContextDisposeRaceTests`, `TransactionContextTests.CommitAndRollback_RaceOnlyOneSucceeds`/`CommitAsync_WithAlreadyCancelledToken_...`). CORE-023's residual TOCTOU is documented as an accepted limitation, not glossed over. |

| DOC-019 | P1 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Reader lease contract | Document EOF auto-disposal, explicit Close/Dispose equivalence, streaming cancellation, command/connection/permit ownership, and what happens when cleanup itself fails. **Closed:** `docs/connection/ownership-and-shutdown.md`'s `ITrackedReader` section already covered Close≡Dispose, ownership, and continue-on-failure cleanup (written earlier this session); added a "Streaming and cancellation" subsection confirming (via `TrackedReader.ReadAsync`'s actual EOF-dispose call and `LoadStreamAsync`/`RetrieveStreamAsync`'s `await using`-inside-the-iterator pattern) that EOF, an early `await foreach` break, and a cancelled token all dispose the reader exactly once, through the same mechanism. |
| DOC-020 | P0 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Context shutdown contract | Define admission closure, active/queued work behavior, drain/cancellation policy, shutdown timeout distinct from acquisition timeout, data-source lifetime, uniqueness-claim lifetime, sync versus async disposal, and the exception returned by every operation attempted after disposal. **Closed (2026-08-29, this session):** `docs/connection/ownership-and-shutdown.md`'s "`DatabaseContext` shutdown sequence" section documents the exact 6-phase order (metrics unsubscribe → persistent connections → open-coordination primitives → close-then-drain both governors → conditional data-source/uniqueness-claim cleanup → base disposal), the corrected fact that drain uses `PoolAcquireTimeout` (not a separate shutdown-specific timeout), the CORE-026 "leak rather than corrupt" policy when a governor times out draining, and confirms sync/async disposal are independently-implemented parallel paths, not one wrapping the other. | DOC-023 | P1 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Portable database-error analysis | `ISqlDialect.ClassifyException` and `AnalyzeException` expose provider-neutral categories, constraint kind, transient/retryable signals, provider code, and SQLSTATE across the dialect family. Current docs mention individual translated exceptions but do not teach this as an application control-flow/observability feature. Document the taxonomy, provider coverage, retry-policy boundaries, examples, and relationship to thrown pengdows exceptions and metrics. **Closed:** new `docs/exception-analysis.md` — the full `DbExceptionInfo` field reference, a concrete per-provider-family error-code/SQLSTATE table (verified directly against `SqlDialect.TryClassifyProviderException`'s actual switch), the relationship table to typed `DatabaseException` subclasses, an explicit note that this and `IDbExceptionTranslator` are two independently-maintained classification systems that can disagree, and an honest retry-policy boundary section (`IsRetryable` tells you whether to retry, it doesn't retry for you — `RetryContext` is designed but not implemented, cross-referenced rather than implied to exist). |
| DOC-024 | P1 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Automatic audit-field lifecycle | Gateways automatically populate `[CreatedBy]`, `[CreatedOn]`, `[LastUpdatedBy]`, and `[LastUpdatedOn]` through `IAuditValueResolver`; batch operations resolve once; timestamps require UTC; user IDs are coerced to target types; `AuditCreationPolicy` controls preservation versus authority; failed writes restore entity audit values. The only discoverable material is an isolated resolver example and positioning prose. Add a complete feature guide and mapping table. **Closed:** new `docs/audit-fields.md` — full CREATE/UPDATE/batch lifecycle, `AuditCreationPolicy`'s security implication (verified against `BaseTableGateway.Audit.cs`'s exact `SetAuditFields` preservation-check code), UTC timestamp validation (`ResolveAuditTimestamp` throws on non-zero offset), user-ID coercion (`Guid.TryParse`/`TypeCoercionHelper`), the batch-resolves-once contract (`ResolveAuditValuesForBatch`, confirmed one `Resolve()` call per batch, reused for every entity), and the snapshot/restore-on-failure mechanism (`SnapshotAuditFields`/`RestoreAuditFieldsIfFailed`). Cross-references `entity-mapping.md`'s attribute-mechanics section and the existing `docs/examples/OidcAuditFieldResolver-example.cs` rather than duplicating either. Doc-only change, no code touched. |
| DOC-025 | P1 | **Closed — moot (2026-08-31)** | Database detection evidence API | `DatabaseDetection.DetectFromConnectionWithDetail` and its genuine async twin return probe evidence, confidence/resolution detail, and failure information. Superseded by CORE-004's revert: this API is `internal` again as of 2026-08-29, so this item is now "design a proper public version" rather than "document the existing one." If revisited, must be paired with moving the contract into `pengdows.crud.abstractions` and sanitizing `FailureReason` (see CORE-004/CORE-005 resolution notes). **Closed:** `FEAT-003` (2026-08-30) closed the underlying question as a deliberate decision, not a deferred task — no public API exists to document, and none should be designed absent a new explicit request. Confirmed still `internal` in `pengdows.crud/internal/DatabaseDetectionService.cs` on the current 3.0 branch. |
| DOC-026 | P1 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Stored-procedure portability | Dialect detection selects `ProcWrappingStyle` and the library contains wrapping strategies for CALL, EXEC, EXECUTE PROCEDURE, Oracle, and PostgreSQL forms. Current docs describe the strategy internally and list scattered support facts, but provide no consumer workflow or cross-provider example. Document construction/execution, input/output/return parameters, wrapping behavior, limits, and the provider matrix. **Closed:** new `docs/stored-procedures.md` — the automatic (`CommandType.StoredProcedure`) and return-value-capture (`WrapForCreateWithReturn`/etc., SQL Server-only) patterns, the exact generated syntax per `ProcWrappingStyle` (verified directly against each `pengdows.crud/strategies/proc/*.cs` file, not re-derived from CLAUDE.md's summary table), named-vs-positional parameter binding, the SQL Server `OUTPUT` marker mechanism (`SqlContainer.WrapForStoredProc`'s `BuildProcedureArguments`), three full worked cross-provider examples (MySQL/Call, Oracle/PL-SQL-block, PostgreSQL read-vs-write), and limits (no multi-result-set traversal, `None`-style engines, return-capture being SQL-Server-only). Doc-only change, no code touched. |
| DOC-027 | P0 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Shared gateway/container template model | `ISqlContainer.Clone()` copies SQL and parameter structure for low-cost rebinding; `Clone(IDatabaseContext)` rebinds the container and parameters to a transaction or tenant context/dialect. The implementation and tests explicitly treat this as essential to cached templates and multitenancy, but no public document mentions the overload. Explain template construction, immutable-versus-mutable state, parameter rebinding, transaction use, tenant use, dialect boundaries, cache reuse, disposal, and safe singleton patterns. **Closed (2026-08-29):** new `docs/sql-container-templates.md`, verified directly against `SqlContainer.Clone`'s source and `SqlContainerCloningTests.cs`. Covers what's deep-copied vs. shared (parameters are always fresh `DbParameter` instances via the target dialect's factory; rendered command text is shared by reference only when already cached), the template pattern with a worked example, transaction use, and disposal independence. **Real nuance found and documented, not assumed:** parameter *markers* re-render correctly per target dialect on `Clone` (since `{P}name` placeholders resolve at first execution using the clone's own dialect) — but identifier quoting from `WrapObjectName` calls is baked into the query text at build time and does NOT re-render per target dialect on `Clone`. This is a non-issue today only because every shipped dialect shares the same ANSI double-quote policy; documented as a real, if currently dormant, hazard for a future non-ANSI-quoting dialect. Also documented the "clone before first execution" caveat for cross-dialect template reuse (a container already executed once caches its rendered text with the *original* dialect's markers baked in, which a subsequent clone would inherit unchanged). |
| DOC-028 | P1 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | SQL-container composition guide | Public fluent helpers quote identifiers and format parameters through the active dialect (`AppendName`, `AppendParam`, fragment helpers), while execution overloads select read/write intent, cancellation, scalar semantics, tracked readers, and `CommandBehavior.SingleRow`. Most appear only in the unindexed `api-supplements.md`; `WrapForStoredProc` and context cloning are absent entirely. Create one discoverable end-to-end guide and link `api-supplements.md` from the docs index or merge it into maintained reference material. **Closed:** new `docs/sql-container-composition.md` covers every fluent helper (verified against `pengdows.crud/SqlContainerExtensions.cs` directly) plus execution-overload selection rules (`ExecutionType`/`CommandType`/`CancellationToken`, including the `ExecuteScalarOrNullAsync()` parameterless-overload-hardcodes-Read footgun this session's CORE-016 work found), and cross-references `stored-procedures.md` (`WrapForStoredProc` — the "absent entirely" gap, now covered by a sibling doc) and `sql-container-templates.md` (context cloning — DOC-027, closed earlier this session, so that framing was already stale). `docs/api-supplements.md`'s "SQL container helpers"/"Gateway and context diagnostics" sections were absorbed into the new guide and replaced with a pointer, resolving the "unindexed" problem; UUID7 byte formats and the declared-but-not-wired-features notes stayed in `api-supplements.md` (out of this item's scope). Still needs a `docs/README.md` Reference-table entry — not added here per this session's fork-coordination convention of not editing shared nav files from parallel workers. |
| DOC-029 | P1 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Streaming query guide | `LoadStreamAsync` and `RetrieveStreamAsync` provide repeatable async streams, cancellation, early-break cleanup, transaction-context execution, and bounded materialization behavior. They are named in the README but only discussed incidentally in internal architecture/performance notes. Document reader ownership, query-per-enumeration semantics, early termination, transaction restrictions, and when to choose list versus stream. **Closed:** new `docs/streaming-queries.md`, verified directly against `BaseTableGateway.Core.cs`/`TableGateway.Core.cs`'s actual `async IAsyncEnumerable<T>` iterator implementations. Documents: query-per-enumeration is real re-execution, not cached replay (each `GetAsyncEnumerator()` call starts a fresh reader); a genuine, previously-undocumented gotcha — the parameterless `LoadStreamAsync(sc)` overload has no `[EnumeratorCancellation]` parameter, so calling `.WithCancellation(token)` on its result silently does nothing, unlike the token-accepting overload; early-break cleanup relies on the iterator's own `await using`, giving the same guarantee as `docs/connection/ownership-and-shutdown.md`'s `ITrackedReader` contract; and the transaction interaction — streaming inside a transaction holds its reader-lock (per this session's `transactions.md` concurrency contract) for the *entire* enumeration, not just the initial query. "Bounded materialization" confirmed to mean simply "one row's worth of state at a time," not a separate prefetch/buffer mechanism. Still needs a `docs/README.md` Reference-table entry — not added here for the same reason as DOC-028. |
| DOC-030 | P2 | **Done (2026-08-30)** | Gateway count helpers | Every gateway exposes `CountAllAsync`, equality/LIKE count, null count, and compound equality-plus-null/not-null count helpers with identifier quoting and parameterization. All four APIs have zero references in public documentation. Add them to the gateway reference with exact limitations: string-valued predicates, supported compound shape, context override, and no general expression system. **Closed:** new `docs/gateway-counts.md` documents all four methods' exact signatures, the SQL each produces, `WrapObjectName`/`AddParameterWithValue` quoting and parameterization, and every limitation (string-valued predicates only, one compound equality+null-state shape, no general filter system, `IDatabaseContext` override supported). Linked from `docs/README.md` and `llms.txt`. **Real behavior gap found during the documentation pass, then fixed via TDD (2026-08-30):** `CountWhereEqualsAsync` used to silently prefer `andWhereNull` over `andWhereNotNull` when both were supplied, with no validation. Fixed: the method now throws `ArgumentException` when both are non-null (test-first — `CountWhereEqualsAsync_WithBothAndWhereNullAndAndWhereNotNull_ThrowsArgumentException` confirmed red, then green after adding the guard clause), and `CountWhereEqualsAsync_WithNeitherAndWhereNullNorAndWhereNotNull_CountsByEqualityOnly` locks in the pre-existing "neither set" behavior as a regression guard. Both `ITableGateway`/`IPrimaryKeyTableGateway`'s XML doc corrected from "exactly one... may be set" to "at most one... may be set" plus an `<exception>` tag. No interface-baseline change (XML doc only, no signature change — 438 signatures, confirmed via regenerate). Full suite green (7472 tests, both net8.0/net10.0). `docs/gateway-counts.md` updated to describe the enforced behavior instead of the old silent-precedence caveat. |
| DOC-031 | P0 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Complete entity-mapping reference | The overview merely names most attributes. It does not teach `[Column]` inclusion/ignore rules, `DbType`, ordinal ordering, writable/generated `[Id]`, composite `[PrimaryKey]` order, JSON serializer options, enum literals/failure policy, insert/update exclusion, audit attributes, correlation tokens, or version behavior as one coherent mapping contract. Create an attribute matrix with read/write behavior, valid combinations, defaults, examples, and gateway compatibility. **Closed (2026-08-29):** new `docs/entity-mapping.md` covers all 15 attribute types with a summary matrix plus per-attribute detail, all verified directly against `TypeMapRegistry.cs`'s actual construction/validation logic rather than restated from CLAUDE.md. Found and documented two real discrepancies between attribute doc-comments and actual behavior while verifying: (1) `[NonUpdateable]`'s own XML doc claims only `[CreatedBy]`/`[CreatedOn]` are "implicitly" non-updateable, but `ColumnInfo.IsNonUpdateable = nonUpd != null \|\| isId` — **every** `[Id]` column (writable or not) is implicitly non-updateable too, not just the two audit attributes; (2) `CreatedBy`/`CreatedOn` exclusion from UPDATE is actually enforced by dedicated `!c.IsCreatedBy && !c.IsCreatedOn` filtering in the gateway SQL builders (`TableGateway.Sql.cs`/`.Batch.cs`), independent of the generic `IsNonUpdateable` flag — the flag itself is never set for those two attributes. Also documented: `[Version]`+`[Json]` mutual exclusivity (JSON silently dropped when both present), `[CorrelationToken]` is `TableGateway<T,TId>`-only, `[Json]` auto-inference is narrow (only `JsonDocument`/`JsonElement`/`JsonNode`/the library's `JsonValue` — not general POCOs/collections), and the exact `SqlGenerationException`/`TooManyColumns`/`PrimaryKeyOnRowIdColumn` throw conditions as a table. Doc-only change; no code modified. |
| DOC-032 | P0 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Runtime database-capability discovery | `IDataSourceInformation` exposes detected product/version, parsed version, quoting, parameter marker/regex/length, named/repeated parameter behavior, parameter/output limits, preparation defaults, procedure style, upsert/merge/truncate/drop capabilities, fallback status, and compatibility warnings. `ISqlDialect` exposes a substantially broader capability surface including batching, namespaces, savepoints, pooling, read-only behavior, modern SQL features, JSON/array/regex/window/CTE/graph support, generated-key strategy, pagination, and exception analysis. Current docs discuss pieces internally but do not teach applications or higher-level Pengdows libraries to query capabilities instead of branching on database names. Provide a public capability reference, stability contract, examples, and provider/version matrix. **Related, confirmed via the same external-document audit as CORE-031/032/034 (2026-08-29):** `ISqlDialect` genuinely mixes three audiences in one 937-line interface — pure capability flags meant for consumer inspection (`SupportsJoins`, `MaxParameterLimit`, `ProcWrappingStyle`) alongside internal SQL-generation machinery only gateway code should call (`BuildBatchInsertSql`, `BuildBatchUpdateSql`, `GetSavepointSql`, `GetLastInsertedIdQuery`, `GetGeneratedKeyPlan`). Confirmed structurally true by direct inspection; whether splitting it into a public capability view plus an internal generation interface is worth the churn is a design call for whoever picks up this item, not a settled conclusion — the interface working today for both purposes at once is a real architectural tension, not a bug in the CORE-* sense. **Closed (2026-08-29, this session):** new `docs/capability-discovery.md` covers how to obtain `context.Dialect`/`context.DataSourceInfo`, makes the two-audience split explicit with a full enumerated list of the internal-machinery members (so a reader knows exactly which ones NOT to call directly), categorizes every consumer-facing `Supports*`/metadata member by purpose (identity, parameters, SQL features, types, constraints, upsert/merge, generated keys, transactions/isolation, stored procedures, batching/pagination, pooling, exception analysis), cross-references `docs/architecture.md`'s capability-derivation section and `docs/supported-databases.md`'s matrix rather than duplicating them, gives a real worked "branch on capability, not database name" example (the PostgreSQL 15+ dual `SupportsMerge`/`SupportsInsertOnConflict` batch-upsert bug from `TableGateway.Sql.cs`'s own inline comment), and states the stability contract honestly — no separate published promise beyond CLAUDE.md naming `ISqlDialect` as official surface area, with the default-interface-method pattern identified as the mechanism that lets new flags be added without breaking existing dialects. |
| DOC-033 | P2 | **Done (2026-08-29)** | Replaceable tenant context factory | `IDatabaseContextFactory` is registered via `TryAddSingleton` in `AddMultiTenancy`, meaning an application can override it by registering its own implementation before calling `AddMultiTenancy` — `TenantContextRegistry` will use it for every context it creates, while tenant resolution and registry lifecycle stay unchanged. Confirmed real via the same external-document audit as CORE-031/032/034 (2026-08-29) — verified the `TryAddSingleton` call site directly. Completely undocumented anywhere. Document: how to replace it, required ownership semantics (does every call need to return a new context? who disposes the returned context — the registry, per its existing lifecycle rules, already does), how provider factories and logger factories flow through, and whether a custom factory may decorate/cache contexts (not recommended without checking `TenantContextRegistry`'s own caching, which would double-cache). **Closed (2026-08-29, this session):** `docs/connection/multitenancy.md`'s "Replacing the context factory" section covers the `TryAddSingleton`/register-before-`AddMultiTenancy` mechanism, the "new context per call, registry owns disposal" ownership contract, and the double-caching warning against a factory that decorates/caches contexts itself. |
| DOC-034 | P2 | **Done (2026-08-30)** | Read-only and contention exception taxonomy | Confirmed via the same external-document audit as CORE-031/032/034 (2026-08-29): there are three distinct read-only-violation exception types — `ReadOnlyContextException : NotSupportedException`, `ReadOnlyAccessException : InvalidOperationException`, and `ReadOnlyViolationException : DatabaseOperationException` — unified by a common `IReadOnlyViolation` marker interface that lets a caller catch all three via `catch (IReadOnlyViolation)`. None of `ReadOnlyContextException`, `ReadOnlyAccessException`, or `IReadOnlyViolation` appear anywhere in CLAUDE.md's Exception Hierarchy section — only `ReadOnlyViolationException` is listed, with no mention it's one of three, or that only it is a `DatabaseException` subclass. Document which layer throws each (configuration-time vs. SQL/provider-rejection-time), which are `DatabaseException` subclasses and which are not (matching the same "not part of the hierarchy" pattern CORE-029 fixed for `PoolSaturatedException`/`ModeContentionException`), the `IReadOnlyViolation` unification pattern, and whether retrying is ever valid for any of them. Also document `PoolForbiddenException : InvalidOperationException` (thrown when a pool with `MaxConcurrentWrites=0`/`MaxPoolSize=0` is accessed) as a related-but-distinct concept — it has no `IReadOnlyViolation` marker since it's an admission-control rejection, not a read-only-mode rejection. **Closed:** all inheritance/throw-site claims above verified directly against source (confirmed accurate). CLAUDE.md's Exception Hierarchy section now has a full "Read-only violations: three exception types, one marker interface" subsection (table of all three + base type + throwing layer, the `IReadOnlyViolation` catch-all example, retry guidance, and `PoolForbiddenException` distinguished as a separate admission-control concept). `docs/read-only-enforcement.md` extended with the same detail in full: a three-way table, a worked `IReadOnlyViolation` catch example, explicit retry guidance (never valid for any of the three — confirmed via `IsTransient = false` and `docs/exception-analysis.md`'s `DbErrorCategory` mapping), and a new "`PoolForbiddenException`: a related but distinct concept" section. No new file/wiring needed — `read-only-enforcement.md` was already linked from `docs/README.md`. |
| DOC-035 | P2 | **Done (2026-08-30)** | Remaining undocumented `MetricsOptions` fields | Partial gap, confirmed via the same external-document audit as CORE-031/032/034 (2026-08-29) — the audit's blanket claim that all of `MetricsOptions`'s controls were undocumented was itself only half right. `EnableApproxPercentiles`/`PercentileWindowSize` are already documented in `docs/metrics.md`. **Still genuinely missing:** `LongConnectionThreshold` and `SlowCommandThreshold` — confirmed zero occurrences of either name anywhere in `docs/metrics.md`. Document what they threshold, their defaults, and how crossing them shows up in recorded metrics (e.g. `LongLivedConnections`, `SlowCommandsTotal`). **Closed:** verified directly against source — `LongConnectionThreshold` (`TimeSpan`, default 30s, must be positive) increments `LongLivedConnections` on connection close when hold duration meets/exceeds it; `SlowCommandThreshold` (`TimeSpan`, default 1s, must be positive) increments `SlowCommandsTotal` on command completion (success or failure) when elapsed duration meets/exceeds it — both surface on `DatabaseMetrics`/`DatabaseRoleMetrics` as cumulative counters, confirmed via `MetricsCollector.cs` and `MetricsCollectorTests.cs`. New "Long-connection and slow-command thresholds" section added to `docs/metrics.md`, matching its existing percentile-tracking section's format. Already-linked doc — no new wiring needed. |

### 4. Verified capabilities that are currently under-explained

These are not speculative roadmap items. They exist in the inspected code or maintained evidence and should be taught explicitly.

| ID | Capability | Evidence/meaning to preserve in docs |
|---|---|---|
| CAP-001 | Runtime provider discovery | Arbitrary ADO.NET provider assemblies can be loaded at runtime without a compile-time provider reference, then registered through keyed DI and `DbProviderFactories`. A provider for a recognized database can receive the database dialect; a wholly unknown engine receives only generic behavior until dialect support is supplied. |
| CAP-002 | Context-per-tenant architecture | Isolation is not a row-filter convention. Each tenant receives an independently governed execution context; database-per-tenant is the deployment model. |
| CAP-003 | Independent admission state | Reader/writer governors, queues, metrics, mode locks, and sentinels are context-owned rather than global. |
| CAP-004 | Tenant registry lifecycle | Lazy singleton context per tenant, concurrent cardinality limit, fault eviction/retry, targeted and global invalidation, and creation/removal events are implemented and tested. |
| CAP-005 | Singleton-gateway safety | Analyzer rules and context propagation protect shared gateways. Binder caches are isolated by dialect instance and SQL templates by capability fingerprint. |
| CAP-006 | Real heterogeneous-version behavior | A maintained integration test uses one shared gateway against MySQL 8.0.19 and 8.0.33, emits the correct version-specific UPSERT, and executes it. |
| CAP-007 | Compile-time guardrails | Analyzers include singleton registration checks, predicate-value parameterization, gateway context propagation, and composite identifier wrapping. |
| CAP-008 | OpenTelemetry lifecycle | Context creation/removal is observed automatically, singleton contexts can be discovered, context IDs correlate traces, and metrics distinguish roles. |
| CAP-009 | Duplicate connection protection | `EnforceUniqueConnectionString` supports warning and hard-reject modes with atomic claims, credential-sensitive hashing without plaintext retention, cleanup, and rollback proof. Reliable tenant-path propagation of this setting was fixed by CORE-001 (2026-08-29) — stale note removed. |
| CAP-010 | Broad database evidence | The maintained testbed records 12 engines and 30 engine/version targets: CockroachDB, DB2, DuckDB, Firebird, MariaDB, MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, SQLite, TiDB, and YugabyteDB. |
| CAP-011 | PDU sentinel model | PreventDatabaseUnload uses held connections as passive sentinels while integrating with context permit accounting. Operational contract fully proven as of 2026-08-29: CORE-002/CORE-003 plus TEST-004 (repair permit-neutrality and provider-pool lifetime stability). |
| CAP-012 | Configuration-native multitenancy | `AddMultiTenancy` binds a complete tenant list, composes per-tenant application names, registers a case-insensitive configuration resolver, a lazy context registry, a replaceable context factory, and keyed-provider resolution. Configurations can also be registered at runtime and contexts invalidated for rotation. **Documented (2026-08-29, see DOC-021):** the "undiscoverable" note is stale — `docs/connection/multitenancy.md` now teaches this as a first-class feature. |
| CAP-013 | Configuration-native provider plug-ins | `AddDbProviderLoading` loads ADO.NET factories by local assembly path, assembly name, or existing `DbProviderFactories` registration, then registers each as a keyed DI singleton and in the legacy registry. This is the mechanism that permits providers unknown at compile time. **Documented (2026-08-29, see DOC-002/DOC-022):** the "absent from the public documentation path" note is stale — `docs/connection/dynamic-provider-loading.md` covers it. |
| CAP-014 | Provider-neutral failure intelligence | Dialects expose both coarse classification and detailed `DbExceptionInfo`: category, constraint kind, transient/retryable flags, provider error code, and SQLSTATE. Shipped translators cover the major supported database families with a fallback path. |
| CAP-015 | Transactional audit-field automation | Entity attributes plus `IAuditValueResolver` drive create/update audit fields, including batch resolution, UTC validation, type coercion, explicit-value policy, and rollback of in-memory mutations when persistence fails. |
| CAP-016 | Evidence-bearing database detection | Public sync and async detection APIs expose not just a product enum but the probes that led to resolution. That is valuable for provider onboarding, diagnostics, and heterogeneous fleets, yet is not presented as a product feature. As of 2026-08-29 (CORE-004) this capability is internal-only again; re-exposing it publicly needs the abstractions placement and sanitization work described there. |
| CAP-017 | Context-rebindable SQL templates | `ISqlContainer.Clone(IDatabaseContext)` preserves a built query and parameter structure while recreating provider parameters for the target dialect/context. Tests cover different dialects, transactions, output parameters, cached command text, and different tenant contexts. This is a core mechanism behind shared gateways, not a minor cloning convenience. **Documented 2026-08-29 — see DOC-027 / `docs/sql-container-templates.md`.** |
| CAP-018 | Dialect-safe explicit SQL composition | `SqlContainerExtensions` supplies a small fluent vocabulary for quoted identifiers, provider-formatted placeholders, common SQL fragments, execution intent, cancellation, and single-row hints without introducing an expression translator. |
| CAP-019 | Lease-safe async entity streaming | Both gateway families can execute arbitrary prebuilt containers as async entity streams, and row-ID gateways can stream ID collections directly. The API explicitly defines re-enumeration, cancellation, and early-break behavior. |
| CAP-020 | Parameterized gateway counts | Both gateway families inherit focused count operations that quote caller-supplied identifiers and parameterize values, covering common operational queries without a general query language. |
| CAP-021 | Attribute-driven persistence policy | The mapping surface does more than property-to-column naming: it controls insertion, updating, generated identifiers, natural/composite keys, audit fields, optimistic versioning, correlation-token key recovery, JSON, enum literals, and deterministic column ordering. |
| CAP-022 | Runtime capability negotiation | The connected context exposes normalized metadata and dialect capabilities rather than forcing consumers to hard-code provider names. This includes syntax, limits, feature support, pooling/read-only constraints, procedure behavior, generated-key strategy, namespaces, isolation, pagination, and compatibility warnings. **Documented (2026-08-29, see DOC-032):** `docs/capability-discovery.md` now teaches this as a first-class feature — `context.Dialect`/`context.DataSourceInfo`, the consumer-vs-internal split, categorized flags, and a worked example. |

### 5. Downstream evidence and adoption paths (not core library)

**pengdows.hangfire**

Treat as downstream transactional proof and an adoption path to pengdows.crud.

Current inspected coverage used live fixtures across 11 engines and shared suites for connections, queues, transactions, locks, expiration, watchdog behavior, and counter aggregation.

Planned after the PC 2.1 release: cleanup and DB2 support, bringing the downstream matrix to 12 engines.

Its claims must remain precise: pengdows bounds and attributes admitted demand. Separate contexts isolate application admission state and provider-pool usage, but cannot eliminate contention for shared physical database resources.

**pengdows.poco.mint and related tooling**

Treat schema-first inspection/generation as an adoption path, not core CRUD functionality.

Current schema inspection is distinct from the proposed generalized, DBA-governed schema executor.

Do not imply that inspecting metadata already provides universal diff planning, dependency ordering, executable DDL, or post-execution verification.

### 6. Product-positioning guardrails

**Goals**

Be the DAL that DBAs insist on.

Be the obvious meaningful choice for relational, database-per-tenant .NET SaaS.

**Defensible central claim**

pengdows.crud combines database-per-tenant deployment with context-per-tenant execution governance, independent admission and telemetry, shared singleton gateways, heterogeneous providers, heterogeneous server versions, runtime provider loading, and real transactional proof through downstream integrations.

**Suggested category statement**

Database-governed, SQL-first data access for relational SaaS.

**Claims to avoid**

"The only meaningful choice for SaaS" without narrowing the category to relational, database-per-tenant .NET systems.

"Pool exhaustion is impossible" or "workloads cannot compete regardless of load."

Implying the library alone provisions one database per tenant or authenticates tenant identity.

Implying arbitrary unknown database engines automatically receive a complete dialect merely because their ADO.NET provider can be loaded.

Treating tests, Hangfire, or generators as code shipped by the two core library projects.

**Open question (not resolved by a code or doc change):** the `crud`-naming/positioning
problem — is "pengdows.crud" the right product name and category framing for the strong
SaaS/DBA positioning claim this section describes, or does the name itself undersell/mismatch
the claim? Surfaced during the 2026-08-12 architecture review, still open as of 2026-08-30. This
is a decision for whoever owns product positioning, not engineering backlog.

### 7. Recommended release sequence

1. ~~Stabilize the contract: CORE-001 and CORE-002~~ — **done**, full test suite green (7441 tests).
2. ~~Correct attribution and security: CORE-003 through CORE-006~~ — **done**.
3. ~~Prove isolation end to end: TEST-001 through TEST-005~~ — **done**, except TEST-005 (superseded/no
   longer applicable per CORE-004's revert). CORE-010's residual race — previously left open as a
   documented, accepted limitation — is now closed too (2026-08-30, via `AcquireLease`/
   `AcquireLeaseAsync`; see its row above).
4. ~~Publish the architecture: DOC-001 through DOC-008 and DOC-011/012~~ — **done.** All of
   DOC-001 through DOC-009, DOC-011, DOC-012, and DOC-014 through DOC-022 are closed (this list
   previously said DOC-005/006/007/009/011/012/015/016/018/019 were still open — that was itself
   stale; every one of those rows closed in the 2026-08-29 doc-backlog passes, this summary just
   hadn't been updated to match).
5. ~~Publish evidence: provider/version matrix and claim-to-test index~~ — **done** (DOC-005/DOC-007,
   2026-08-29).
6. ~~Strengthen downstream proof: Hangfire cleanup~~ — **done** (DOC-013, 2026-08-30, in the separate
   `pengdows.hangfire` repo). DB2 addition to that README remains deliberately deferred until after
   the PC 2.1 release, per DOC-013's own completion criteria — not part of this step's scope.
7. ~~Expand the DBA story: design the generalized schema executor as a separate, reviewable,
   DBA-authorized capability~~ — **done** (DOC-010, 2026-08-30, `docs/schema-management-boundary.md`
   — documents today's inspection/adoption boundary and the future executor's pipeline design as an
   explicitly unimplemented concept, not a built feature).

### 8. Definition of ready for the 2.1 claim

The release is ready to make the strong SaaS/DBA positioning claim when:

- ~~every P0 core issue is closed~~ — **true as of 2026-08-30**: CORE-010, the last open P0, is
  closed via `AcquireLease`/`AcquireLeaseAsync` (leased-handle API, see its row above) — the
  leased-handle redesign previously judged out of scope was revisited once the user reframed live
  tenant rotation as a requirement, not a nice-to-have;

  unit tests, 30/30 testbed engines, 192/197 integration tests, all green);
- ~~two-tenant failure containment is directly proven~~ — **true** (TEST-001);
- ~~tenant configuration copying cannot silently drift again~~ — **true** (CORE-001, with a
  reflection-based completeness regression test);
- ~~runtime provider loading and its limits are first-class documentation~~ — **true** (DOC-002/022);

  responsibility~~ — **true** (DOC-001/014, `multitenancy-architecture.md`'s enforcement table);

  `docs/positioning/implementation-evidence.md`, closed 2026-08-29);
